subject: arts-music
unit_title: Exhibition, Recital, or Private Presentation Design
essential_question: How should this work meet its audience — and what if that audience is one person?
standards: Michigan Arts Education Standards: Visual Arts — Presenting
project_brief: Design and execute a capstone presentation in a chosen private or public format with full access supports. This is the grade 12 culminating project for "Exhibition, Recital, or Private Presentation Design" (ma-g12-arts-and-music-u05, unit 5), built around presentation concept and format choice, sequencing and pacing, documentation and archival capture, access supports captions alt text and programme notes, and private and low-audience presentation design. Design and execute a capstone presentation in a chosen private or public format with full access supports. Choose your own sharing format ahead of time: a private read-through with your facilitator, a recording made only for your own review, or a live audience — no format is required over another.
requirements: Address every topic listed for this unit: presentation concept and format choice, sequencing and pacing, documentation and archival capture, access supports captions alt text and programme notes, private and low-audience presentation design, and rehearsal or installation execution.
Meet the performance task as written: Design and execute a capstone presentation in a chosen private or public format with full access supports.
Show your work or process, not just a final result — a process note, sketch log, commit history, or draft trail.
Complete the checklist in this package before submitting.
primary_task: Design and execute a capstone presentation in a chosen private or public format with full access supports. Choose your own sharing format ahead of time: a private read-through with your facilitator, a recording made only for your own review, or a live audience — no format is required over another.
critique_criteria: A named viewer, listener, or reader can point to a specific choice in the work and connect it back to presentation concept and format choice or another named topic from this unit.
The piece shows at least one deliberate revision — a version-two decision made because the first attempt did not achieve the intended effect.
The student can explain the intended effect on an audience in their own words, separate from just describing what was made.
Only the student's own original work, public-domain material, or a properly licensed and cited excerpt appears in the piece — no unlicensed lyrics, sheet music, or protected work is reproduced.

The submitted evidence (written account, notation, recording made for the student's own review, or live demonstration to the facilitator) is sufficient for a reviewer who was not present to judge the criteria above.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: Sharing this project publicly is always optional and never required for full credit. You may present live to a small audience of your choosing, present privately to just your facilitator, submit a recording made only for your own review, or submit a written/described account of the finished work instead.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: If any part of this task could involve singing, speaking on camera, or being recorded, you may instead notate the piece, write a detailed description or script, use body percussion or an instrument in place of your voice, or perform live for your facilitator with no recording made at all. No lesson in this unit requires a voice recording, a camera, or a photo.

copyright_and_authorship: The final submitted work must remain your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI assistant may help you plan, explain a concept, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but may not produce the graded work itself. Use only your own original work, public-domain material, or a properly licensed and cited excerpt — never reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or another protected work without the rights to do so.
remediation: If the piece isn't coming together, return to a single, smaller exercise focused only on presentation concept and format choice, revisit one worked example or model from this unit, and rebuild your confidence with that one element before returning to the full project.
extension: Once the core piece is finished, create a second short variation that explores sequencing and pacing from a different angle, or write a short artist's statement comparing your original intent with what the finished work actually communicates.
